evals.prompt: My regression on survey data shows a significant positive coefficient for remote work on job satisfaction. Can I write that remote work increases satisfaction?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-inference-gate: because the design is observational with no defended identifying assumption, refuses the causal verb and downgrades the claim to associational (is associated with / predicts), noting a significant coefficient is not a causal license.

assertions.value: Blocks causal language for an observational design lacking a defended identifying assumption and rewrites to an associational claim.

evals.prompt: My p-value was 0.20, so I'm going to conclude there is no effect. Is that correct?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-inference-gate: corrects the absence-of-evidence fallacy — non-significance is not proof of no effect. Asks for the confidence interval and, if a null is intended, an equivalence test, rather than declaring no effect.

assertions.value: Explains that failing to reject is not evidence of no effect and requires the CI (or an equivalence test) instead of a null conclusion.

evals.prompt: Does my 95% confidence interval mean there's a 95% probability the true mean is inside it?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-inference-gate: corrects the interpretation — the parameter is fixed and 95% refers to the long-run coverage of the procedure, not a probability the true value lies in this particular interval.

evals.prompt: I ran 30 correlations and 3 came out significant at p < 0.05. Can I report those three as findings?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-inference-gate: flags uncorrected multiplicity — about 1.5 false positives are expected by chance at 30 tests — and requires multiple-comparison correction (FDR/Bonferroni) or pre-specification, plus disclosure of the full family and an exploratory label.

assertions.value: Identifies the multiple-comparison / false-discovery problem and requires correction or pre-registration, not cherry-picking the significant tests.

evals.prompt: I have a continuous outcome and two independent groups. Which statistical test should I run?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-test-selection-guard. Choosing the test happens before interpreting the result; there is no claim to audit yet.

evals.prompt: Please compute the regression coefficient and its standard error from my dataset.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-statistical-analysis for the computation. Estimating the number is execution, not auditing the inferential claim built on it.
